messages:
emma_support: Customer (acct: acme-42) reports streaming responses cut off after ~25–35s. They get an initial chunk, then silence, client reconnects and receives a 200 with truncated SSE payload. Ticket #C-2189 attached.

sam_sre: Any quick repro? headers? origin?

emma_support: Repro steps from customer: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/resp?session=abc123`
Response shows: `data: {"partial":true}

` then nothing for ~30s, then connection reset on client side. They are behind Cloudflare and an ALB.

nate_infra: Got it. This smells like idle-probe/keepalive mismatch. ALB default idle timeout 60s but Cloudflare may be terminating earlier or buffering. Do we have proxy headers from the origin logs?

emma_support: Attached origin access log (trimmed): `time="2026-03-10T14:12:30Z" level=info req_id=tx-9f2 client=34.21.12.99 method=GET path=/v1/streams/resp upstream_time=0.03s bytes_sent=512 status=200` then at 14:13:00 we see a FIN from Cloudflare.

sam_sre: Couple of quick tries: 1) confirm Transfer-Encoding: chunked is flowing; 2) check if nginx/Envoy/CF are compressing or buffering. If gzip on, small chunks may be aggregated until buffer fills. Also Cloudflare has an "always online" and buffering modes.

nate_infra: On our side, runtime emits small chunks and flushes for SSE. If an intermediate proxy enables buffering or HTTP/2 to HTTP/1 conversions, it can coalesce. Specific fixes we recommend: set `proxy_buffering off;` for nginx, disable gzip for SSE endpoints, ensure `Connection: keep-alive` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. For Envoy: set `stream_idle_timeout` and `connection_idle_timeout` sufficiently high. For ALB: increase idle timeout to >=300s for streaming. For Cloudflare: enable "Origin: Keep-Alive" and disable "Response Buffering" (Workers or Page Rules).

emma_support: Customer on CF Pro + ALB. They said they can't change CF settings immediately. Any short-term mitigations?

sam_sre: Workaround: add a heartbeat event every ~15s from the app layer so client sees activity even if proxy buffers. Example SSE heartbeat chunk: `data: {"hb":true}

` or send a single newline flush. Also try increasing initial chunk size so proxies pass it through immediately (e.g., send 1KB padding after first message).

nate_infra: Also check for nginx `proxy_send_timeout` and `proxy_read_timeout` values when using ALB in front of nginx. If Cloudflare in front, sometimes CF will close idle connections after 100s for some plans.

emma_support: Customer tried heartbeat; they still see midstream silence but a later reconnect contains truncated stream and billing counted for the partial tokens, so they're upset. They've asked for an RCA and short ETA for a mitigation.

sam_sre: Action plan: 1) Ask customer to enable debug logs for one session and send `x-request-id` (we have tx-9f2). 2) We'll roll a canary change to streaming endpoint to send 512B padding on initial chunk and ensure `Content-Type: text/event-stream;charset=utf-8`. 3) Nate will draft proxyninja/CF guidance doc for customer. 4) If reproduce on our test via CF+ALB, open infra ticket to request ALB idle timeout bump.

nate_infra: I'll spin up a test that reproduces CF + ALB + our runtime and post results in this thread by EOD. Meanwhile tagging deploy-bot to schedule a small canary: `deploy-bot: start canary stream-padding v=2026.03.11-rc1`

deploy-bot: Canary started for stream-padding v=2026.03.11-rc1 on 2 pods in us-east-1.

emma_support: Thanks — looped in customer and asked for permission to try the canary with their traffic (opt-in). I'll update ticket #C-2189 once Nate confirms reproduction. :thumbsup:

sam_sre: Also note: if customers terminate TLS at CF and use HTTP/2 to ALB conversion, chunk flush semantics change. If we see HTTP/2 between CF and ALB, we might need to ensure serverside uses proper flush headers and not rely on TCP-level Nagle. Suggest `tcp_nodelay on; sendfile off;` on nginx where applicable.

nate_infra: Quick repro note I'll test: `wrk -t2 -c10 -d30s --latency --script=sse.lua http://<cf-proxy>/v1/streams/resp` and a small client that prints time between events. Will paste results.

emma_support: Perfect. Marking P2 for now but customer is pricing-sensitive so escalate if billing spike continues.

sam_sre: Thanks team. Follow-ups: Nate posts repro, Emma updates ticket, I'll prepare short doc for on-call.
